let's execute this: I've just pushed a new branch — feature/env-switching — that fixes a problem we've all hit: juggling .env values by hand every time you switch between dev/test/sit/uat/staging. It's not in a PR yet, I want a few of you to actually run it first and tell me if it breaks on your machine before I open one.
 
What it does, quickly:
- One command scaffolds all your local env files and pulls in whatever's already shared with the team
- Switching tiers is now one line instead of copy-pasting values around
- It'll actually tell you if something's misconfigured (wrong host, blank token, etc.) instead of you finding out the hard way mid-checkout-flow
 
Can you pull it and run through this?
 
Markdown
git fetch
git checkout feature/env-switching
npm ci
npm run env -- init
 
That last one will scaffold your local env files and pull in anything already shared. It'll probably flag a few things as blank — some of those are yours to fill in personally (your own Contentful token, your own Jira/Confluence login if you use those), so don't panic if you see warnings, just read what it's telling you.
 
Then:
 
Markdown
npm run env -- validate
 
Should come back clean (or close to it). If it flags an actual ERROR rather than just "blank," that's worth flagging to me.
 
The bit I really want tested — does it actually connect to anything real:
 
Markdown
npm run env -- dev
npm run env -- validate --live
 
That second command doesn't just check your files look right, it actually calls Contentful and SFCC for real and tells you if the credentials genuinely work. If you see OK next to both for the dev tier, we're good. If you see an ERROR, that's exactly the kind of thing I need to know about.
 
Last step — just run npm start after switching to a tier and make sure the site actually boots and pulls real data like normal.
 
Try switching to a different tier too (npm run env -- sit or whichever) and see if that feels sane.
 
No pressure to be thorough — just want a sanity check from a couple of you before this goes any wider. Ping me here or DM if anything's confusing or breaks.

let's execute this: I've just pushed a new branch — feature/env-switching — that fixes a problem we've all hit: juggling .env values by hand every time you switch between dev/test/sit/uat/staging. It's not in a PR yet, I want a few of you to actually run it first and tell me if it breaks on your machine before I open one.
 
What it does, quickly:
- One command scaffolds all your local env files and pulls in whatever's already shared with the team
- Switching tiers is now one line instead of copy-pasting values around
- It'll actually tell you if something's misconfigured (wrong host, blank token, etc.) instead of you finding out the hard way mid-checkout-flow
 
Can you pull it and run through this?
 
Markdown
git fetch
git checkout feature/env-switching
npm ci
npm run env -- init
 
That last one will scaffold your local env files and pull in anything already shared. It'll probably flag a few things as blank — some of those are yours to fill in personally (your own Contentful token, your own Jira/Confluence login if you use those), so don't panic if you see warnings, just read what it's telling you.
 
Then:
 
Markdown
npm run env -- validate
 
Should come back clean (or close to it). If it flags an actual ERROR rather than just "blank," that's worth flagging to me.
 
The bit I really want tested — does it actually connect to anything real:
 
Markdown
npm run env -- dev
npm run env -- validate --live
 
That second command doesn't just check your files look right, it actually calls Contentful and SFCC for real and tells you if the credentials genuinely work. If you see OK next to both for the dev tier, we're good. If you see an ERROR, that's exactly the kind of thing I need to know about.
 
Last step — just run npm start after switching to a tier and make sure the site actually boots and pulls real data like normal.
 
Try switching to a different tier too (npm run env -- sit or whichever) and see if that feels sane.
 
No pressure to be thorough — just want a sanity check from a couple of you before this goes any wider. Ping me here or DM if anything's confusing or breaks. - report back when done with implementation and sanity check / safety audit

## Phase
**Detailed Design** — Some functional requirements have been confirmed (30 Apr 2026 sign-off); others are still open. No production build has started beyond scaffolding.

Workshop sign-off tracker: All workshops signed off (2026-04-30 through 2026-06-24). Row-level opens tracked under Unresolved Dependencies below.

*For system roles and integration details, see [architecture.md](architecture.md). Open items that block implementation are listed under "Unresolved Dependencies" below.*

## Integrations

Global-e handles shipping/duties/taxes at international checkout via vendor cartridge + iframe injection. REG-040 struck (superseded by REG-041, confirmed). |

Six-tier topology reference at [Environment Topology & Promotion Path](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304840708) (Confluence). Pending: SFCC SIT credentials, `MRT_SIT_URL` / `MRT_TEST_URL` GitHub Secrets, `push:sit` / `activate:sit` npm scripts, `mobify.config.js` `sit` env entry, `config/sit.js`. |

| Narvar | Not started | |

| Avalara | Not started | Covers US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, **and EU domestic** (confirmed 2026-06-19 via Third_Party_Integrations sheet update). UK uses SFCC native VAT tables. |

| Inside Chat | Not started | |
| Transperfect | Not started | Direct Contentful↔Transperfect workflow confirmed (REG-047 update); SFCC strings via JSON files. PWA only consumes translated payloads |
| Google Business API | Not started | Daily store-hours feed into SFCC; PWA renders only (out-of-band) |
| Feedonomics | Not started | Product feed for downstream marketing channels (PRD-071); no PWA runtime touchpoint |

## What's Complete
- PWA Kit scaffolding with TypeScript strict mode (`@salesforce/retail-react-app` bumped from v9.1.1 → v10.0.0 on 2026-05-18)
- Overrides pattern established
- Country/locale config (`overrides/app/config/countries.ts`)
- Contentful Studio integration (pointing to mock account)
- **Contentful content type sync script** (`npm run sync:contentful`) — upserts content types from `scripts/contentful/content-types/` via the Management API.
- **ShoppableImage component** — Experience Builder component + standard content type. React component at `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/shoppableImage.tsx`. Content type definition at `scripts/contentful/content-types/shoppableImage.js`. Content type synced to Contentful (mock space) 2026-05-11.

- **Header visual refinement**: layout and animations are implemented; still being iterated against the draft Figma to close remaining gaps

- All integrations need to point to production accounts (SFCC, Contentful)
- Global-e integration (confirm pricing flow mechanism before implementing)
- Didomi consent management (implement per storefront defaults in REG-054)
- Omneo / Emarsys marketing sync

- MuleSoft middleware connections

- Address autocomplete via Google Maps API
- Narvar EDD + tracking integration
- SEO: hreflang, canonical URLs, sitemaps
- Order-on-behalf (OOBO) for CS agents
- Retail Rewards (AP21) integration
- Gift card PDP, cart, checkout, and GiveX integration
- Promotions engine and multi-currency/FX pricebook setup

  - `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): `unit-tests` (Vitest) + `storybook-test` (Storybook `play` + `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `storybook test --ci`) run in parallel; `e2e-browserstack` on release PRs only. **`storybook-test` job is wired but pending `@storybook/addon-test` and `@storybook/addon-a11y` installation (feature/storybook-v10 upgrade task).**
  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)

- Product copy ownership: Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 (TBD).
- Translation trigger workflow with TransPerfect (TBD).
- Global-e + Didomi consent interaction (TBD).
- **Social login (Apple/Google):** Confirmed in scope for launch (ENH-004, Must-Have, Go-Live) as SFCC OOTB configuration only. **Hard dependency:** Apple and Google merchant accounts must be provisioned by Zimmermann before implementation can start. Do not implement until merchant accounts exist.
- **Omneo guest record creation timing:** When to create an Omneo record for a guest (at newsletter sign-up, at back-in-stock capture, at checkout, or only at order completion) is under legal/SFCC best-practice review. #     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
#     automatically. Placed before the Contentful check's early exit (below)
#     so it always runs regardless of whether component files are staged.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'

  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1d. .env.sample secret guard — BLOCKS the commit if a var whose name looks
#     like a secret (TOKEN/SECRET/KEY/PASSWORD/CREDENTIAL) has a non-empty
#     value staged in .env.sample. Real values belong only in .env (gitignored)
#     — see AGENTS.md > Rules > Environment variables. Checks the staged
#     (index) content, not the working tree, and runs before the Contentful
#     check's early exit below so it always executes.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  leaked_vars=$(git show ':.env.sample' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^[A-Z0-9_]*(TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL)[A-Z0-9_]*=.+$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$leaked_vars" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains non-empty secret-shaped value(s):"
    echo ""
    echo "$leaked_vars" | sed -E 's/=.*/=<redacted>/' | sed 's/^/       /'
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only ever contain blank placeholders for TOKEN/SECRET/KEY/"
    echo "  PASSWORD/CREDENTIAL variables (see AGENTS.md > Rules > Environment variables)."
    echo "  Move the real value(s) to your local .env (gitignored) and blank them here."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Contentful definition drift check
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

WARNINGS=0

# Staged .jsx/.tsx files scoped to components/ or ui/ directories only
staged_components=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '(components|ui)/.*\.(jsx|tsx)$' \
  | grep -v 'ContentfulDefinition' \
  || true)

[[ -z "$staged_components" ]] && exit 0

echo ""
echo "Checking for Contentful definition drift..."

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  dir=$(dirname "$file")
  base=$(basename "$file")
  base="${base%.*}"
  def_file="${dir}/${base}ContentfulDefinition.ts"

  # Only warn if a definition file exists
  [[ ! -f "$def_file" ]] && continue

  # Warn if the definition is not also staged alongside the component
  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF "$def_file"; then
    echo "  ⚠️  $(basename "$file") — definition not staged: $def_file"
    WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS + 1))
  fi
done <<< "$staged_components"

if [ "$WARNINGS" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  $WARNINGS component(s) may have stale Contentful definitions."
  echo "  Run /contentful-drift-check to review, then stage any updated definition files."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derived configuration file guard
#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

blocked_files=()

# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  # Only check files in derived locations
  case "$file" in
    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac

  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue

  # Extract the first source path from the synced-from comment
  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2] — ... -->
  # or:     <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md — ... -->
  synced_from=$(echo "$synced_line" \
    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//' \
    | sed 's/,.*//' \
    | tr -d ' ')

  [[ -z "$synced_from" ]] && continue

  # If the source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
  # update — the developer edited the .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
  # Skip it.
  if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF "$synced_from"; then
    continue
  fi

  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
  blocked_files+=("$file")

done <<< "$modified_staged"

if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
  echo ""
  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
    echo "       $bf"
  done
  echo ""
  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
  echo ""
  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
  echo ""
  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  secret_violations=()

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a JWT
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
      continue
    fi

  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)

  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
    echo ""
    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
      echo "    $v"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
    echo ""
    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

exit 0

## Ran the full test plan

Everything executed cleanly:

- **`npm ci`** — succeeded (2,740 packages). Pre-existing deprecation/audit-vulnerability noise is unrelated to this branch.
- **`npm run env -- init`** — idempotent; files already scaffolded, GitHub Environments pull reported "already up to date" across all 7 scopes (no local edits got clobbered).
- **`npm run env -- validate`** — clean: no errors, no warnings, only blank-value counts (expected — most integrations aren't provisioned yet).
- **`npm run env -- dev`** — switched correctly, `ENVIRONMENT_NAME`/`DEPLOY_TARGET` stamped as expected.
- **`npm run env -- validate --live`** — **both live checks passed**: Contentful Delivery API and SFCC SLAS guest-token exchange both came back "OK" for dev, test, sit, uat, and staging.
- **`npm run env -- sit`**, then back to **`dev`** — clean tier switching each time.
- Edge cases: no-arg reports current tier cleanly; an unknown tier name fails loudly with usage help and exit code 1 (no silent bad state).
- **`npm start`** — **not run**, per AGENTS.md's explicit "Do not run!" rule. Run it yourself (or type `!npm start` here) — but see the finding below first.
- **`push`** — **not run** (writes real values to a shared GitHub Environment — out of scope for a sanity check, and you'll want the finding below fixed before anyone pushes from dev/sit/test).

One minor hiccup: `init`'s Contentful auto-fetch failed ("access token you sent does not have access to the requested resource"). That's this machine's personal `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` lacking access to space `u9kb6gp6slxu` — a personal-credential problem, not a tooling bug. The script degraded gracefully (logged it, didn't crash).

## Critical finding — dev/sit/test OCAPI host is broken, and it's already centrally shared

This branch's commits changed the OCAPI proxy host in `config/dev.js`/`config/sit.js` (and the new `config/test.js`) from hyphens to underscores:

| Tier | `develop` (correct) | this branch (broken) |
|---|---|---|
| dev | `bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com` | `bkzk_002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com` |
| sit | `bkzk-003.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com` | `bkzk_003.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com` |
| test | *(file didn't exist before)* | `bkzk_005.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com` |

I DNS-resolved both forms: every hyphenated host resolves to real SFCC ingress IPs; every underscored one returns **nothing** — underscores aren't valid DNS-label characters, so these hosts simply don't exist. The OCAPI proxy target for three tiers is unreachable.

It's worse than a local typo: `gh variable list --env dev/sit/test` confirms the same broken value is **already pushed to the shared GitHub Environments** — exactly what everyone you ask to run `npm run env -- init` will pull down.

Why didn't `validate` or `validate --live` catch it? The static cross-check compares the env value against `config/<tier>.js` — but both sides already carry the *same* broken value, so there's nothing to diff. The live SFCC check only exercises the SLAS endpoint (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`), a completely different hostname — it never touches `COMMERCE_API_OCAPI_HOST` at all. So the tooling behaved exactly as designed; it just has no live check that could have caught this specific break, and the break itself is a real defect in this branch's other commits, not in the env-switching logic.

I didn't touch `config/dev.js`, `config/sit.js`, or `config/test.js` — that's a Tier 1 directory, and a full fix also means deciding whether to re-push corrected shared values, which affects everyone's config. I confirmed via `gh` that this session is already recognized as a tier-1-approver, so I can fix all three files and walk through re-pushing corrected values if you want — just say the word.

## Safety audit of `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`

- **No command injection** — the only `execSync` calls that interpolate a variable (`scope`) do so only after it's validated against a fixed allow-list; untrusted input never reaches the shell.
- **No secret leakage** — live-check errors surface only HTTP status/network-error text, never the token itself.
- **Personal credentials handled correctly** — both `push` and `init`'s pull explicitly exclude `scope:personal` keys (Contentful CMA token, Atlassian tokens) in both directions.
- **The `.env.sample` secret guard is real and doubly redundant** — `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` blocks a commit on both secret-shaped key names and value-shape heuristics (JWT/hex/base64/provider prefixes), independently, both exiting 1 on violation.
- **`.gitignore` covers every tier file exactly**, matching the script's own tier list — nothing can slip through uncommitted-but-tracked.
- **Worth restating despite being an already-accepted tradeoff**: real secrets get pushed as plaintext GitHub *Variables* (not *Secrets*) — readable by any repo collaborator, not just workflow runners. The code comments call this a deliberate, confirmed (2026-07-13) override of AGENTS.md's normal secrets policy. Not relitigating it, just flagging it since it's the single biggest deviation from your standard secrets policy in this tooling.
- **Gotcha, not a bug**: `init`'s GitHub pull silently *overwrites* a local value that differs from the remote one (not just fills blanks) — by design, remote wins. If you hand-tweak a shared/tier value locally, a later `init` will quietly revert it (it does log `update KEY`, easy to miss in a long run).
- **No CI coverage** of this script at all — fine for local-only tooling, but a no-credentials-needed `npm run env -- validate` smoke test in CI would catch a future structural regression for free. Optional.
- **Governance note**: this branch spans Tier 1 (`config/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CODEOWNERS`) and Tier 2 (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `protectedFiles.md`) files in one PR. CODEOWNERS is wired correctly for both, so both approver groups will be required on review — worth calling out in the PR description so it's not a surprise.

## Bottom line

The tooling itself is solid — idempotent, degrades gracefully, no injection/secret-leak issues, real guardrails. But there's a live, already-centrally-shared bug underneath it (dev/sit/test OCAPI hostnames) that this test plan's live checks can't see. I'd fix that before asking more people to pull the branch — right now, anyone following your exact steps gets a silently-broken OCAPI proxy for three tiers.

content.text:
Recapping from the audit, in priority order:

**1. Must-fix — broken OCAPI host (the critical one)**
`config/dev.js`, `config/sit.js`, and the new `config/test.js` have the OCAPI proxy host typo'd with an underscore instead of a hyphen (`bkzk_002` vs. the real `bkzk-002`, etc.). DNS-confirmed: the hyphenated form resolves to real SFCC ingress, the underscored form resolves to nothing. It's already pushed to the shared `dev`/`sit`/`test` GitHub Environments, so it's not just a local mistake — everyone who runs `npm run env -- init` inherits it.

**2. Coverage gap that let #1 slip through — `validate --live` never touches the OCAPI host**
The live check exercises SLAS (via the SCAPI shortcode domain) and Contentful, but nothing hits `COMMERCE_API_OCAPI_HOST` itself. A tier can report "OK" on both live checks while its OCAPI proxy is completely unreachable. Worth adding a lightweight reachability check (DNS resolve or HTTP HEAD) against that host per tier, alongside the existing two.

**3. Related design blind spot — the static cross-check only catches *drift*, not *wrongness***
`validate`'s comparison of `.env.<tier>`'s `COMMERCE_API_OCAPI_HOST` against `config/<tier>.js` only flags a mismatch between the two. If both are wrong in the same way (as happened here, since the bad value was pushed centrally and then pulled back down to match), there's nothing to diff against. This is inherent to a consistency check rather than a bug, but pairing it with #2 (an actual reachability check) closes the gap.

**4. Gotcha — `init` silently overwrites local values that differ from the remote**
Not a bug, but worth tightening: pulling from GitHub Environments will overwrite an existing non-blank local value if it differs from what's centrally stored (only logs `update KEY`, easy to miss in a long run). A louder callout when this happens would reduce surprise.

**5. Optional — no CI coverage of the script itself**
Nothing in `.github/workflows/` runs `switchEnv.mjs` at all. A no-credentials-needed `npm run env -- validate` smoke test in CI would catch a future structural regression (like a malformed `.env.sample`) for free. Not blocking since it's local-dev tooling.

**6. Worth flagging, not necessarily changing — secrets stored as GitHub *Variables*, not *Secrets***
Real credentials pushed via `gh variable set` are plaintext, readable by any repo collaborator (not just workflow runners). This is already a deliberate, documented, confirmed tradeoff (2026-07-13) for centralization — not something I'd change unprompted — but if the team ever wants to revisit it, that's the concrete mechanism to swap (`gh secret set`), with the caveat that secrets can't be read back for diffing the way `pullFromGitHubEnvironments` currently does, so that function would need a rework too.

Items 1–3 are the ones I'd actually act on before this goes wider; 4–6 are polish/process, not blockers.

content.content:
1	# 01 — Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI) + reCAPTCHA
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (SFCC) is the system of record for commerce data. The storefront calls SFCC directly from the browser via SCAPI for browsing, basket management, customer accounts, and order placement.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Authentication via Shopper Login & API Access Service (SLAS)
10	- Product catalogue, categories, search, recommendations
11	- Basket and cart
12	- Customer account (authentication record) and saved-payment token references
13	- Order placement for SFCC-owned checkouts (domestic markets)
14	- Gift cards — the storefront applies them via SCAPI; server-side redemption is outside the PWA boundary
15	- Google reCAPTCHA — browser-side script load on register/login forms; MRT-side token verification before SCAPI submission
16	
17	At migration, only the customer's email and Omneo ID are stored in SFCC. Name, phone, addresses, and communication preferences come from Omneo at login (DMU-004). Order history comes from MuleSoft via the MRT proxy, not from SFCC (DMU-007).
18	
19	Out of scope of this document:
20	
21	- GiveX validate/redeem/refund, Avalara tax, Adyen back-office — all server-side, outside the PWA
22	- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft flows to NewStore, AP21, Omneo, Narvar
23	- Booxi appointment booking — MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a SFCC flow
24	- Business Manager configuration: promotions rules, content slots, Page Designer pages
25	
26	## 2. Browser-side architecture
27	
28	```
29	PWA (React, SSR + CSR)
30	        │
31	        │  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
32	        ▼
33	SLAS auth (guest or registered shopper) ──► Shopper context
34	        │                                       (site, currency, locale, customer)
35	        ▼
36	SCAPI: products, search, baskets, orders, customers, promotions, gift cards
37	        │
38	        ▼
39	SFCC realm
40	```
41	
42	- **Single SDK.** `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` handles every SFCC call — SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching.
43	- **SSR and CSR.** Catalogue, PDP, PLP, content, and boutique pages are server-rendered for SEO and LCP. Cart, checkout, My Account, and order pages render an SSR shell and hydrate personalised data client-side after auth.
44	- **Managed Runtime.** The PWA Kit Node layer hosts the SSR pipeline and routes SLAS private-client calls through the server-side proxy.
45	
46	## 3. Authentication and credentials
47	
48	- **SLAS private-client flow** issues two token types: a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper access token (issued after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs with a customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and refresh token.
49	- **Refresh tokens live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies** set by the SSR layer. Browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token. On each refresh SLAS regenerates the token and voids the old one; the SSR layer rewrites the cookie in the same response.
50	- **Private client credentials.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser. The authorisation code exchange goes through the MRT private-client proxy (`privateClientProxyEndpoint`). The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code stay in the bundle as public identifiers.
51	- **Social login.** Apple and Google via SLAS third-party identity-provider federation — confirmed in scope for launch; implementation design still open.
52	- **No Open Commerce API (OCAPI) credentials in the browser.** Any operation not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through Managed Runtime with OCAPI credentials held server-side.
53	
54	### Magento password migration (CFD-013)
55	
56	Passwords were not migrated from Magento. All existing customers must reset at go-live. Failed sign-ins return a generic "invalid credentials" message (no email-existence leak) and the "forgot password" link is always visible.
57	
58	### Cross-storefront session continuity
59	
60	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single domain and share one SFCC realm.
61	
62	- **The refresh-token cookie is shared across storefronts.** Every storefront lives on the same domain, so the `httpOnly` cookie is sent on every path prefix. No cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
63	- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A token issued for `zimm-au` is not valid for `zimm-uk` — this is a hard SLAS platform constraint. On a storefront switch the SSR layer performs a fresh authorisation for the destination channel using the SLAS Trusted System on Behalf (TSOB) flow: it calls `getTrustedSystemAccessToken` with the shopper's `login_id`, which issues a new channel-scoped token server-side without prompting the customer. A registered shopper stays signed in transparently. A guest session does not carry over — guest tokens and baskets are site-scoped. **TSOB rate limit:** SLAS returns HTTP 409 if multiple TSOB calls are made for the same shopper within a 3-second window — the SSR layer must not fire duplicate TSOB calls on rapid storefront switches (debounce or dedupe at the MRT layer).
64	- **Baskets do not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency. Switching storefront starts a fresh basket; carrying one across a currency boundary would produce wrong prices.
65	- **Checkout handoff is a separate boundary.** When handing off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into Global-e's hosted checkout.
66	
67	## 4. Data exchanged
68	
69	| Resource                           | Verbs                    | Notes                                                                                                                                           |
70	| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
71	| `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | GET, POST                | SLAS authentication and token lifecycle                                                                                                         |
72	| `/product/shopper-products/v1/*`   | GET                      | Product details, master/variant resolution                                                                                                      |
73	| `/search/shopper-search/v1/*`      | GET                      | Catalogue search, faceting, sort, suggestions                                                                                                   |
74	| `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*`   | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Basket lifecycle, line items, shipments, payment instruments                                                                                    |
75	| `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*`    | POST, GET                | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts only)                                                                                          |
76	| `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | GET, POST, PATCH         | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references                                                                                                    |
77	| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | GET                      | Active promotions, coupon validation                                                                                                            |
78	| Einstein recommendations endpoints | GET                      | Personalised recommendations slot. Consent-gated (Didomi purpose TBC) — falls back to a static SFCC merchandising group if consent is not given |
79	
80	Every request carries the site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and SLAS bearer token. PII travels over TLS only. PCI scope is Adyen's — SFCC holds token references only.
81	
82	## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)
83	
84	- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
85	- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
86	- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
87	- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.
88	
89	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
90	
91	- **HTTP/2** to a single SCAPI host; `<link rel="preconnect">` emitted in the document head.
92	- **TanStack Query** dedupes in-flight requests. Working defaults: stale time 60 s for catalogue, 30 s for promotions, 0 s for basket (always fresh).
93	- **SFCC edge cache** for anonymous catalogue traffic; cache keys include site, locale, currency, and customer group.
94	- **Parallel calls on PDP.** Product, recommendations, and promotions are fetched in parallel — no waterfall.
95	- **SSR fetches only critical data.** Recommendations and reviews load client-side after hydration.
96	- **Field projection.** SCAPI `fields=` parameters are used where supported to reduce payload size.
97	
98	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
99	
100	SFCC site IDs and Business Manager locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 Business Manager (2026-06-13):
101	
102	| SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                                  | URL prefix                                 | Currency               | Checkout owner              |
103	| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------- |
104	| `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                                          | `/` (root, x-default hreflang)             | AUD                    | SFCC                        |
105	| `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                                       | `/us/`                                     | USD                    | SFCC (US domestic)          |
106	| `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(TBC)_                               | `/en-ca/`                                  | USD                    | Global-e (US international) |
107	| `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                                       | `/uk/`                                     | GBP                    | SFCC                        |
108	| `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB` (EN), `fr` (FR), `it` (IT), `es` (ES) | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR                    | SFCC                        |
109	| `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                                       | `/en-ch/`                                  | EUR                    | Global-e                    |
110	| `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                                       | `/hk/`                                     | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
111	| `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                                       | `/en-ae/`                                  | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
112	
113	- The site ID is resolved from the URL prefix on every request (SSR and CSR).
114	- AU is geo-redirected for non-Oceania human visitors; verified search bots and social unfurlers are exempt via UA allowlist.
115	- Per-environment SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain outstanding — see §11 item 2.
116	
117	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
118	
119	| Failure                                       | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                       |
120	| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
121	| SLAS unavailable                              | Storefront cannot mint a guest token and is non-operational. Show a maintenance message. P1 incident.                                                                           |

# 01 — Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI) + reCAPTCHA

## 1. Purpose and scope

Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (SFCC) is the system of record for commerce data. The storefront calls SFCC directly from the browser via SCAPI for browsing, basket management, customer accounts, and order placement.

In scope:

- Authentication via Shopper Login & API Access Service (SLAS)
- Product catalogue, categories, search, recommendations
- Basket and cart
- Customer account (authentication record) and saved-payment token references
- Order placement for SFCC-owned checkouts (domestic markets)
- Gift cards — the storefront applies them via SCAPI; server-side redemption is outside the PWA boundary
- Google reCAPTCHA — browser-side script load on register/login forms; MRT-side token verification before SCAPI submission

At migration, only the customer's email and Omneo ID are stored in SFCC. Name, phone, addresses, and communication preferences come from Omneo at login (DMU-004). Order history comes from MuleSoft via the MRT proxy, not from SFCC (DMU-007).

Out of scope of this document:

- GiveX validate/redeem/refund, Avalara tax, Adyen back-office — all server-side, outside the PWA
- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft flows to NewStore, AP21, Omneo, Narvar
- Booxi appointment booking — MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a SFCC flow
- Business Manager configuration: promotions rules, content slots, Page Designer pages

## 2. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (React, SSR + CSR)
        │
        │  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
        ▼
SLAS auth (guest or registered shopper) ──► Shopper context
        │                                       (site, currency, locale, customer)
        ▼
SCAPI: products, search, baskets, orders, customers, promotions, gift cards
        │
        ▼
SFCC realm
```

- **Single SDK.** `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` handles every SFCC call — SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching.
- **SSR and CSR.** Catalogue, PDP, PLP, content, and boutique pages are server-rendered for SEO and LCP. Cart, checkout, My Account, and order pages render an SSR shell and hydrate personalised data client-side after auth.
- **Managed Runtime.** The PWA Kit Node layer hosts the SSR pipeline and routes SLAS private-client calls through the server-side proxy.

## 3. Authentication and credentials

- **SLAS private-client flow** issues two token types: a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper access token (issued after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs with a customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and refresh token.
- **Refresh tokens live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies** set by the SSR layer. Browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token. On each refresh SLAS regenerates the token and voids the old one; the SSR layer rewrites the cookie in the same response.
- **Private client credentials.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser. The authorisation code exchange goes through the MRT private-client proxy (`privateClientProxyEndpoint`). The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code stay in the bundle as public identifiers.
- **Social login.** Apple and Google via SLAS third-party identity-provider federation — confirmed in scope for launch; implementation design still open.
- **No Open Commerce API (OCAPI) credentials in the browser.** Any operation not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through Managed Runtime with OCAPI credentials held server-side.

### Magento password migration (CFD-013)

Passwords were not migrated from Magento. All existing customers must reset at go-live. Failed sign-ins return a generic "invalid credentials" message (no email-existence leak) and the "forgot password" link is always visible.

### Cross-storefront session continuity

All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single domain and share one SFCC realm.

- **The refresh-token cookie is shared across storefronts.** Every storefront lives on the same domain, so the `httpOnly` cookie is sent on every path prefix. No cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A token issued for `zimm-au` is not valid for `zimm-uk` — this is a hard SLAS platform constraint. On a storefront switch the SSR layer performs a fresh authorisation for the destination channel using the SLAS Trusted System on Behalf (TSOB) flow: it calls `getTrustedSystemAccessToken` with the shopper's `login_id`, which issues a new channel-scoped token server-side without prompting the customer. A registered shopper stays signed in transparently. A guest session does not carry over — guest tokens and baskets are site-scoped. **TSOB rate limit:** SLAS returns HTTP 409 if multiple TSOB calls are made for the same shopper within a 3-second window — the SSR layer must not fire duplicate TSOB calls on rapid storefront switches (debounce or dedupe at the MRT layer).
- **Baskets do not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency. Switching storefront starts a fresh basket; carrying one across a currency boundary would produce wrong prices.
- **Checkout handoff is a separate boundary.** When handing off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into Global-e's hosted checkout.

## 4. Data exchanged

| Resource                           | Verbs                    | Notes                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | GET, POST                | SLAS authentication and token lifecycle                                                                                                         |
| `/product/shopper-products/v1/*`   | GET                      | Product details, master/variant resolution                                                                                                      |
| `/search/shopper-search/v1/*`      | GET                      | Catalogue search, faceting, sort, suggestions                                                                                                   |
| `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*`   | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Basket lifecycle, line items, shipments, payment instruments                                                                                    |
| `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*`    | POST, GET                | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts only)                                                                                          |
| `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | GET, POST, PATCH         | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references                                                                                                    |
| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | GET                      | Active promotions, coupon validation                                                                                                            |
| Einstein recommendations endpoints | GET                      | Personalised recommendations slot. Consent-gated (Didomi purpose TBC) — falls back to a static SFCC merchandising group if consent is not given |

Every request carries the site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and SLAS bearer token. PII travels over TLS only. PCI scope is Adyen's — SFCC holds token references only.

## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)

- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **HTTP/2** to a single SCAPI host; `<link rel="preconnect">` emitted in the document head.
- **TanStack Query** dedupes in-flight requests. Working defaults: stale time 60 s for catalogue, 30 s for promotions, 0 s for basket (always fresh).
- **SFCC edge cache** for anonymous catalogue traffic; cache keys include site, locale, currency, and customer group.
- **Parallel calls on PDP.** Product, recommendations, and promotions are fetched in parallel — no waterfall.
- **SSR fetches only critical data.** Recommendations and reviews load client-side after hydration.
- **Field projection.** SCAPI `fields=` parameters are used where supported to reduce payload size.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

SFCC site IDs and Business Manager locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 Business Manager (2026-06-13):

| SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                                  | URL prefix                                 | Currency               | Checkout owner              |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                                          | `/` (root, x-default hreflang)             | AUD                    | SFCC                        |
| `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                                       | `/us/`                                     | USD                    | SFCC (US domestic)          |
| `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(TBC)_                               | `/en-ca/`                                  | USD                    | Global-e (US international) |
| `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                                       | `/uk/`                                     | GBP                    | SFCC                        |
| `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB` (EN), `fr` (FR), `it` (IT), `es` (ES) | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR                    | SFCC                        |
| `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                                       | `/en-ch/`                                  | EUR                    | Global-e                    |
| `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                                       | `/hk/`                                     | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
| `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                                       | `/en-ae/`                                  | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |

- The site ID is resolved from the URL prefix on every request (SSR and CSR).
- AU is geo-redirected for non-Oceania human visitors; verified search bots and social unfurlers are exempt via UA allowlist.
- Per-environment SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain outstanding — see §11 item 2.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure                                       | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SLAS unavailable                              | Storefront cannot mint a guest token and is non-operational. Show a maintenance message. P1 incident.                                                                           |
| SCAPI catalogue 5xx                           | TanStack Query retries three times with exponential backoff. On final failure, show the last cached payload if available; otherwise show an error state with a "Try again" CTA. |
| SCAPI basket 5xx during add-to-cart           | Inline error toast. The user's intent stays in client state so a retry resends the same request.                                                                                |
| Order placement 5xx after Adyen authorisation | Hard error — the order cannot fail silently. The customer sees an explicit error with a contact reference and ops is alerted.                                                   |
| Einstein recommendations 5xx                  | Hide the slot or fall back to a static merchandising group.                                                                                                                     |
| SLAS token refresh fails                      | Force re-login. The basket is preserved on the guest token until the customer completes checkout.                                                                               |
| TSOB 409 (rapid storefront switch)            | Retry after 3 seconds. Do not re-login the customer — the existing session is still valid on the origin channel.                                                                |
| reCAPTCHA fails to load or token rejected     | Block the register/login submit, show a "please retry" message, and offer a contact-support path after two failures.                                                            |

## 9. Security and privacy

- All traffic is TLS 1.2+ over HTTPS.
- SLAS private-client flow — the authorisation code exchange is proxied through MRT so the client secret never reaches the browser.
- Refresh tokens are held in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies — never in browser JavaScript.
- PCI scope is Adyen's — the browser sends payment data directly to Adyen. SFCC holds token references only.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.

2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) holds `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl`'s origin in a pool separate from `sfcc-scapi` (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). That separation only provides blast-radius isolation if the two hosts are different origins. If `sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to the same SCAPI host, the pools should be merged.

All findings hold up under independent re-verification — nothing needed retracting, and I found one methodology gap in my own earlier check that's now closed. Here's what changed:

**OCAPI host bug — now confirmed via 4 independent methods, not just one `dig +short`:**
- Full (non-`+short`) `dig` shows the authoritative response directly: hyphenated host → `NOERROR`, resolves via CNAME to real SFCC ingress. Underscored host → **`NXDOMAIN`** — the authoritative server explicitly says the domain doesn't exist, not a timeout or resolver hiccup.
- Cross-checked against two independent public resolvers (Google `8.8.8.8`, Cloudflare `1.1.1.1`) for all three tiers — same result every time, ruling out any local/corporate DNS quirk.
- Cross-checked via a completely different resolution path (`curl`'s OS-level `getaddrinfo`, not `dig`'s own protocol implementation) — hyphenated host connects and gets a real HTTP response (404, but a real server answered); underscored host fails at `curl: (6) Could not resolve host` before any connection is even attempted.
- **New corroborating evidence I hadn't cited before**: `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` §7, written 2026-06-13 (weeks before this branch existed), independently documents *"verified against **bkzk-002** Business Manager"* — hyphenated, from an unrelated integration spec, not from anything touched by this branch. That's a second, independent human source confirming the hyphen is the real identifier.

**Already-pushed-to-shared-config claim** — re-queried `gh variable list` for dev/sit/test (and uat/staging for contrast): identical results, bad value confirmed still live centrally.

**No live check covers OCAPI** — re-confirmed via an exhaustive grep of every `OCAPI`/`ocapi` occurrence in the file, not just my earlier reading; there is no live-check function referencing it anywhere.

**No command injection** — re-checked repo-wide (not just this one script); found two more `execSync` sites elsewhere in `scripts/`, both using either static strings or filesystem-derived paths, no unvalidated external input in any of them.

**gh identity / tier-1-approver status** — independently re-ran the membership check myself rather than trusting the script's own printed claim. Confirmed: `marcelannavarro` is a member. Side finding: `TimLavelleACC` (the branch's commit author) is *also* a tier-1-approver — so this wasn't a review bypass, just an ordinary typo that happened to slip past the one check that could've caught it.

**Pre-commit secret guard — this is the one claim I hadn't actually nailed down before, and now have**: I'd only read `scripts/hooks/pre-commit`'s content, not confirmed it actually *runs*. **No CI coverage** — re-ran with a broader, case-insensitive net; the only hit was `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, a synced docs file, not a workflow. Conclusion unchanged.

One precision note for how I phrase the writeup: I can state with certainty that the configured hostname doesn't exist in DNS (proven four independent ways). I'd keep the "so it breaks OCAPI-proxied calls" part framed as a well-supported consequence rather than an observed crash, since I haven't run the app — `01-sfcc.md` §3 confirms OCAPI proxying is real, live server-side infrastructure MRT depends on for anything not yet on SCAPI, so the consequence is solid, just not something I watched fail in a browser myself.

content.text:
Good catch to push on — and the answer is more interesting than a simple yes/no: **it was intentional, but the reasoning behind it looks wrong.**

The commit message for `5f4da82` (the commit that made this change) is explicit:

> "Also fixes pre-existing config/\<tier>.js gaps this surfaced: ... and corrects the dev/sit/test SFCC OCAPI hosts to use underscores (bkzk_00N) instead of hyphens, **matching the real sandbox hostnames**."

So this wasn't a fat-finger typo — it was a deliberate "fix," described as a correction *away from* hyphens *toward* underscores, on the belief that underscore was the real format. That directly conflicts with what I verified by DNS: the hyphenated form is what actually resolves to real SFCC infrastructure; the underscored form doesn't exist in DNS at all (`NXDOMAIN`, confirmed on multiple resolvers). So the change was intentional, but the premise behind it appears to be factually incorrect.

I think I can explain how that belief formed. `.env.sample` (and every `.env.<tier>`) has:
```
COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID=f_ecom_bkzk_002
```
That's a genuinely, correctly underscore-separated identifier — Salesforce's org-ID format really does use underscores (`f_ecom_{realm}_{instance}`). But that's a *different* identifier from the OCAPI proxy *hostname* (`bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com`), which is a real DNS name and must use a hyphen — DNS doesn't allow underscores in hostname labels. Same "bkzk" + "002" tokens, two different SFCC-defined formats, sitting a few lines apart in the same file. That's a very easy pattern-match to get backwards, especially skimming the file rather than checking DNS.

Worth flagging: all three commits on this branch carry `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5`, so a prior Claude Code session is the one that made this specific "correction" and wrote the confident-sounding justification into the commit message. That's a good reminder that an AI-authored claim in a commit message is still just a claim — it needed the same DNS check to hold up, and here it didn't.

This doesn't change the recommendation — the DNS evidence is independent of anyone's stated intent — but it does change how the finding should be *worded*. "Typo" was the wrong characterization on my part; it's more accurate to say the hostname format was confused with the org-ID format. Want me to update the draft report to Tim with that correction?
